description: Bag (multiset) cross-language conformance — the MIDDLE rung of the algebra ladder (G-Set ⊂ Bag ⊂ Z-set; 081KSXN940008QG0R00171YAZW bus / 081KSXN940008QG0R0033T2BQT observe-algebra). A Bag is the Z-set restricted to NON-NEGATIVE multiplicity (weight codomain ℕ): every key carries a count >= 1 and the combiner is per-key SUM (per the database-design ADR 2026-05-31 — Bag = ℕ/sum). The load-bearing contrast with the G-Set: G-Set union is set-union, hence idempotent; Bag union is a commutative MONOID, NOT a semilattice — union(a, a) DOUBLES every count (the `notIdempotent` law below). Every impl starts from `initialBag`, replays `ops` in order under the canonical key comparator, and must value-match `expectedReplayStates[i]` after op i AND `expectedFinalState`. Bags serialize as ascending-key-sorted { e, n } entries (n >= 1, no key twice), so equality is array-equality. Oracle #1 = TS reference; F#/C#/Rust join later per the meet-in-the-middle 4-oracle.
comparator: ascending Unicode code-point order on the key `e` (matching UTF-8 byte order).

ops.note: NON-idempotent: existing key, count 2 → 3 (the Bag/G-Set distinction)
sum combiner over unsorted input: b-001 1→3, b-003 0→1, b-005 3→4
identity: union with the empty bag is a no-op
addN: new key at count 5, sorted to the front

laws.associative: union(union(a, b), c) == union(a, union(b, c))
laws.notIdempotent: union(a, a) doubles every count (== scale a by 2) — the Bag/G-Set distinction
